**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject runs with failed live writes**

When a preliminary GET fails, a PATCH returns non-200, or a 200 response cannot be decoded, the write is omitted from `Expected`; the verdict checks only delivered observations and observer attachment, not `WritesAnswered == WritesAsked`. Consequently, a run with fewer than the required 200 writes and 10,000 observations can still report plain `"met"`. Treat every unsent or unsuccessful write as a failed expected observation and prevent a passing verdict.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Match the updated row by task ID**

When another visible task has the same generated title and already has the desired state, this watcher resolves before the PATCH is reflected and records an artificial near-zero delivery time. The launch fixture generates 5,000 task titles from only 100 verb/noun combinations, so duplicate titles are expected; identify the row using the task ID encoded in its link or another stable DOM attribute rather than title text.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject samples whose response body was incomplete**

When a response returns 2xx headers and `io.ReadAll` subsequently fails, `client.do` stores the failure in `apiSample.Err`, but this branch still adds its server and partial round-trip times to the successful sample set. A run containing truncated focus, task, table, graph, or write responses can therefore report a target as `met`; treat a nonempty `s.Err` as a failed attempt and exclude it from the latency distribution.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Do not reuse a later arrival for multiple writes**

When the writable-task sequence revisits a task and an observer misses an earlier invalidation, the same later arrival satisfies every preceding write because it is never consumed and `a.Version >= w.Version`. Since these writes toggle state, an arrival for a later `todo` version can falsely count as delivery of an earlier `doing` write that was never observed, allowing all expected observations and a passing verdict despite a missing update. Match each arrival to at most one write, or verify the expected state/version for each write.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Fail material verification when its database read fails**

If the verifier connection drops or this query otherwise fails after the initial connection succeeds, the discarded `Scan` error turns the result into `0/0`. The material PATCH can still be recorded as a successful sample and the “50 watching supporters” target can be reported as `met` even though the harness never verified its workload; propagate the query error into a failed sample or abort the run instead of treating it as zero.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Scope candidate verification to the material change**

During the API run, session goroutines concurrently perform comment replies and task changes, both of which can insert their own `ok_alert_candidates`, so this organization-wide count can change between `before` and `now` for reasons unrelated to the watched-source PATCH. A valid material change will then be classified as `unverified` whenever unrelated candidates make `added != total`, preventing the material target from passing under the intended concurrent workload; count only `flow_source_changed` candidates attributable to this change or its supporter tasks.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Exclude undersized pages from the 25-slice target**

When pagination reaches a terminal page containing fewer than 25 slices, this branch records its size but leaves the sample successful, so `classify` includes its server time in the target named "table page of 25 slices." Whenever `TotalSlices` is not divisible by 25, the benchmark can therefore report `met` using latency samples from a smaller workload; mark non-25-slice responses as unverified for this target or restart pagination before timing them.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Reject malformed table responses**

When `/flow/table` returns HTTP 200 with a complete but invalid JSON body, this branch leaves `s.Err` empty, so `classify` treats the response as timed and its server latency can contribute to a `"met"` table target; `TablePages` merely records zero slices and `targetVerdict` never checks that count. Record the decode error so malformed pages fail closed rather than becoming successful measurements.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Stop waiting for network idle while the event stream is open**

In the real web composition, `session.tsx` starts the persistent `/api/v1/events` fetch while the workspace is loading, and `source.ts` keeps reading its response body until the session ends. Consequently, `home()` cannot reach Playwright's `networkidle` state and each readiness, frame, or live measurement times out here before collecting samples. Wait for a finite application-ready condition instead of global network idleness.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Serialize batched refetches like the web client**

When a focus refetch lasts until the next invalidation batch—possible with the default 1.5-second write interval even near the 2-second target—`flush` clears `timer` before doing its network reads, so the next event starts another `AfterFunc` callback and refetch concurrently. The real client serializes these refreshes through `LiveBus.run` and `useFlowTable`'s `serial` queue; allowing the harness's second refetch to bypass the first can make later observations complete much earlier and produce a passing p95 that the client would miss. Keep the batch marked as running and queue one follow-up flush instead.

### 🛡️ Codex Security Review · _Automatically triggered_

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub> Security: Bound Flow audit fan-out per request**

When Flow is enabled, an ordinary member can prepare 100 owned focuses with 200 tasks each and repeatedly request `/api/v1/flow/table?limit=100`. This new loop converts that one read token into at least 41 separate `Guard.Release` calls; each opens/commits a transaction and appends a 500-item audit row. The default limiter permits 600 reads/minute plus a 100-request burst per replica, while these rows are append-only and retained for a year, so a member can monopolize the API DB pool and grow durable audit storage until OKR is unavailable. Production is currently default-off, so impact is conditional, but staging is on. Cap total items/batches per response or charge limits by audited items.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Drain in-flight requests before ending measurement**

When a session starts its final request shortly before `end`, this deadline cancels the request exactly at the measurement boundary; because its `Sent` timestamp is still before `end`, the canceled request is retained as a measured failure. With 50 randomly phased sessions, requests whose legitimate latency overlaps the cutoff can therefore make an otherwise valid run permanently `incomplete, not met`, since every target requires zero failures. Stop scheduling new work at `end`, but allow already-started requests to finish under the caller's context before building the report.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Propagate tenant query errors**

If this startup query fails after the transaction has opened—for example because the connection drops—the error is discarded and the returned `rows` is passed to `pgx.CollectRows`; this can panic on a nil rows value or obscure the actual database error instead of returning it from `readTenant`. **<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Parallelize focus reads within a live refresh**

When invalidations for multiple focuses accumulate while an earlier refresh is running, this loop waits for each focus request before starting the next. The real client’s `useFlowTable.refreshFocuses` starts the named focus reads together with `Promise.all`; only `LiveBus.run` serializes successive refresh batches. The harness therefore measures the sum rather than the maximum of those request times and can report that the 2-second live target was missed even though the browser meets it. Preserve the outer queue serialization, but issue the focus reads within one refresh concurrently.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Verify acknowledgements clear the source flag**

When the acknowledge endpoint returns a valid task object but fails to record all supplied source versions, `checkTask` accepts the response solely because its ID matches, so that request is included as a successful timed `flow_acknowledge` sample even though `source.flagged` remains true. This can let the writes target pass without measuring completed acknowledgements, especially for the final material cycle, which has no subsequent change to expose the failed reset. **<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Count acknowledgements skipped at the cutoff**

When a measured material PATCH finishes near or after `end`—for example, after a delayed cycle causes the beat to catch up—`rctx` is already expired, so these goroutines return without sending or recording some or all of the 50 acknowledgements. The material sample remains successful, and the writes target sees neither failures nor missing attempts, allowing both targets to report `met` with part of the declared workload omitted; either stop starting material cycles that cannot finish their acknowledgements or record every skipped acknowledgement as a failed attempt.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve the operation timestamp across prerequisite reads**

When a task-write tick begins just before `end` and its prerequisite GET finishes after `end`, the PATCH still runs, but this call records `r.sent`, so `record` classifies the write outside the measurement window. **<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Require all three numbered frame runs**
